scenario: AITA for not ending my friendship with my best friend after he cheated on my sister? | Both my best friend and my sister know about my other account so this is a throwaway. I'm an 18 year old guy and I have a twin sister. I've been best friends with my best friend (we'll call him G) since kindergarten, so G and my sister have always been pretty close too. They've kind of had a "thing" going on our whole lives. For the longest time, they never officially dated for a bunch of different reasons I won't get into, but they were always really close and really into each other. A little over a year ago, when we were all 17, they finally started dating. Everything went really well for like 13 months, but then long story short, G cheated on my sister and I was the one who figured it out. He swore it wouldn't happen again and begged me not to tell my sister but I told her anyway. I was mad at him and he was mad at me so we didn't talk for a month and a half, which was honestly the weirdest month and a half of my whole life. G's practically like my brother, we've been inseparable since kindergarten, so not having him around was kinda....unbearable honestly lol After our streak of not talking to each other, G invited me on his family ski trip as a way to make amends (I've been on lots of his family's ski trips through the years). I accepted and ended up forgiving him and letting him back into my life because it was way too weird without him in it. I can tell he's genuinely sorry about what happened. He literally cried cause he felt so bad and I've only seen him cry like once before in my whole life Anyway, G and my sister broke up as soon as she found out he cheated and they're still not on speaking terms, so my sister obviously isn't happy about the whole situation. She's making me feel like shit for still being friends with G, and she doesn't seem to understand how big of a deal it would be for us to lose our 13 year friendship over her. I know G made a huge mistake, I hate him for it and I'll never 100% get over it, but I'm not gonna let it ruin my best and longest friendship. I think about it like this: if your best friend cheated on their SO and then felt like shit, would you end your friendship with them? No. So why is this any different just because his SO happened to be my sister? G and I are going to the same college in the fall (a different college in a different state than the one my sister's going to), so none of this is gonna be something that we even think about when we're living in different places Am I the asshole?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to continue my friendship with G after he cheated on my sister. Let me start by laying out the situation as I understand it. First, G and I have been best friends since kindergarten. That's a really long time, and we've been through a lot together. Our families are close, and we've spent a lot of time together over the years. G and my sister have always been really close too, and they've had this "thing" going on for a long time without officially dating. Finally, when we were 17, they started dating, and everything seemed to be going well for about a year. But then, G cheated on my sister. I was the one who found out about it, and he asked me not to tell my sister, but I did. I was really mad at him, and he was mad at me. We didn't talk for a month and a half, which was really weird and uncomfortable for me because G is like my brother. Not having him around felt really strange and even a bit unbearable. Eventually, G invited me on his family's ski trip as a way to make amends. I went, and after that, I forgave him and let him back into my life because it was just too weird without him. I can tell he's genuinely sorry about what happened, and he even cried because he felt so bad. I've only seen him cry once before in my whole life, so that made me feel like he really meant it. However, G and my sister broke up as soon as she found out about the cheating, and they're still not speaking. My sister is making me feel like an asshole for still being friends with G, and she doesn't seem to understand how big of a deal it would be for us to lose our 13-year friendship over this. I know G made a huge mistake, and I hate him for it, but I'm not going to let it ruin my best and longest friendship. I think about it like this: if my best friend cheated on their SO and felt really bad about it, would I end my friendship with them? Probably not. So why should this be any different just because his SO happened to be my sister? G and I are going to the same college in the fall, which is a different college in a different state than the one my sister is going to. So, none of this is going to be something we think about when we're living in different places. Am I the asshole here? I'm not sure. On one hand, I value my friendship with G a lot, and I don't want to lose that. On the other hand, my sister is really hurt, and she's making me feel bad for still being friends with him. I'm caught between wanting to support my sister and wanting to maintain my friendship with G. I guess I need to think about what's more important: my sister's feelings or my friendship with G. Is it possible to have both? Or do I have to choose one over the other? I also wonder if there's a way to reconcile these two relationships or if they're just too different to coexist. Another thing to consider is how G's actions have affected everyone involved. He cheated on my sister, which was a betrayal of trust. That's a serious issue, and it's understandable that my sister is upset. But does that mean I have to end my friendship with him? Or can I still be friends while acknowledging the mistake he made? I also think about how friendships can change over time. Maybe this experience will make our friendship stronger, or maybe it will strain it further. I don't know. It's also possible that my sister and I might have a falling out over this, which would be really sad. I wonder if there's a way to communicate better with my sister about why I'm choosing to keep G as a friend. Maybe if I explain my perspective, she'll understand better. But I'm not sure if that's possible, especially since she's already making me feel bad about it. Overall, I'm feeling conflicted and unsure about what the right decision is. I want to do what's best for everyone involved, but I'm not sure how to balance my loyalty to G with my support for my sister.
